children: U.S. soybean futures edged lower on Thursday, following a decline in crude oil prices, though expectations of firmer demand from top buyer China helped limit losses.
Wheat and corn futures also traded lower.
FUNDAMENTALS
* The most-active soybean contract
on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was down 0.11% at $13.19 a bushel, as of 0056 GMT. Soyoil (BOcv1) lost 1.21% to 68.83 cents per pound, tracking lower crude oil prices.
* Wheat
fell 0.34% to $7.28-1/4 a bushel and corn
dropped 0.19% to $5.33-1/4 a bushel.
* Soybeans and corn often track crude oil prices because of their use in biofuel production.

* Traders were awaiting an expected meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington next week, which could offer greater clarity on future Chinese demand for U.S. soybeans.
* U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that he planned to meet his Chinese counterpart this weekend.
* Rain in parts of the upper Midwest has delayed harvesting, lending some support to corn prices, analysts said.

* Traders continued to assess risks to grain exports from the Black Sea region. Russian air strikes damaged buildings in Kyiv and injured three people in the Black Sea port city of Odesa early on Thursday, Ukrainian officials said.
* Jordan's state grain buyer has issued an international tender to buy up to 120,000 metric tons of milling wheat that can be sourced from optional origins, European traders said.
* Canadian farmers will produce 11% less wheat and about the same amount of canola as they did last year, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday in its first crop production report of 2026.
* Commodity funds were net sellers of CBOT corn and soybean futures, traders said on Wednesday. (CBOT/FUNDS)
